 Learn more Investing.com -- Morgan Stanley told clients in a note Monday that several upcoming clearing events, including the midterm elections, should mark the end of the current equity correction. 
 Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list » 
 Strategist Michael Wilson said markets have been adjusting to a mid-cycle transition since June. Slowing growth in the Fed's balance sheet, capital scarcity and the midterms have exacerbated that adjustment, while quality has consistently led during the shift and is now breaking out. 
 Morgan Stanley's tactical downside target for the S&P 500 is 7,100 to 7,200, a slight break of the 200-day moving average. Its year-end base case remains 8,000. 
 The bank identified three clearing events. The first is AI-related concerns about the supply and cost of capital, safety and NIMBYism, which should come to a head over the next three to four weeks. 
 The second is the midterm elections. 
 "Midterm elections are typically a market headwind initially and usually then lead to very strong 6-12 month returns post the event," Wilson wrote. 
 Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks » 
 He cautioned that the path could be messy and may linger for days or weeks after election day. 
 The third is tightening financial conditions, driven by Fed rate hikes, slower balance sheet growth and higher energy prices. 
 "Of all the concerns, we think liquidity presents the biggest risk and catalyst for a final low," the strategist said. 
 Wilson noted that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh took office with a strong commitment to returning inflation to 2%, but the Fed has hiked only once since. 
 Back-end rates have risen more than 100 basis points since February. He said this tightening could slow growth and inflation, but it could also cause market stress that leads to a Fed pivot. 
 "That would be asset price bullish in the short term even if it implies a more extended path to reaching the Fed's inflation goals," Wilson said.
